result.strongest_objection: Item 3 is closed as 'REFUTED' (§1 row 3, §3.4) on the strength of a measured timing margin (0 collisions in 40 runs, worst margin 216.9 ms) for a fail-closed startup gate, even though the doc's own forced reproduction (V18) shows a real collision refuses BOTH profiles — a user-facing startup outage — and R1 admits the exclusion holds 'by measured ordering, not by a lock.' R1's 'Not proposed' analysis evaluates exactly one enforcement design (a cross-profile barrier with per-early-return signaling) and rejects it as a larger concurrency surface, but never evaluates the structurally simpler alternative: hoisting the `net6 := newProbeListener()` bind out of `probe()` (`:455`) into `ProbeExecProfilesEach` before the goroutine fan-out (`:224-229`), which makes the exclusion invariant hold by construction with zero signaling and no deadlock surface. With no enforcement, no successor row (§3.4: 'There is no successor row for the in-process case'), and only the §3.5 log-watch trigger as mitigation, the doc leaves a demonstrated nondeterministic cross-profile false-refusal path open on a fail-closed startup check — contrary to the mission's deterministic-behavior axiom — while declining the one cheap structural fix without considering it.
result.catch: In §8 R1, the reopen vector is 'a future edit that moves newProbeListener later in probe()' — i.e., the invariant is guarded by nothing but the current statement order and a 40-run measurement. Before accepting 'REFUTED, no code,' verify whether the bind can be hoisted into `ProbeExecProfilesEach` (one listener per profile allocated before `go func()` at `:226`, handed into `probeExecProfile`, closed by a parent-level defer on error paths at `:369-401`), which would delete the reopen vector entirely; and note the separate, lesser flag: T11 pins `c.resume()` — a line the doc's own V5/V10/V12 evidence shows is host-visibly inert on the only measured platform — via an exact source-string match, so if item 2's disposition stands as structural-only, that should be an explicit, acknowledged trade in the quorum, not silently carried by an S6 label.
result.proposed_fix: Revise §3.4 and R1 to one of: (a) add P4 — hoist the per-profile net6 bind into `ProbeExecProfilesEach` ahead of the fan-out so port exclusion across profiles is structural rather than measured, with a verification-log row demonstrating K-style mutation (moving the bind back after a slow pre-bind step) reds a test or is impossible by construction; or (b) if the hoist is judged out of scope, demote the item-3 verdict from REFUTED to 'refuted at HEAD by measurement; enforcement residual open,' open a tracked successor row for the hoist, and add a comment at `:455`/`:226` stating the ordering invariant the code relies on — since the current text ships a known double-refusal failure mode (V18) guarded only by the §3.5 `accepts N≥2` watch trigger that fires after a startup refusal has already occurred.
